bull.t: Strong revenue growth and gross margins
bull.b: Revenue reached about $240M TTM while gross margins stayed near 89–91%, showing strong product economics and rapid commercial scaling. However, the high-margin profile has not yet translated into earnings because operating costs remain substantially above gross profit.

Q2 sales rose 19% sequentially, reimbursed patients grew more than 20% quarter over quarter, and the U.S. launch generated over 400 start forms. These indicators support expanding physician adoption and payer access, which can broaden the treated rare-disease population over coming quarters.

IMCIVREE has European authorization for acquired HO, with Japan and European launches planned, while RM-718 and bivamelagon advance toward later-stage development. Patent protection extending past 2040 could support a durable franchise if trials and launches succeed.

bear.b: TTM operating margin was roughly -77% and net margin roughly -86%, despite strong revenue and gross margins. Persistent large losses indicate commercialization has not reached operating leverage, leaving profitability dependent on substantial future growth and expense discipline.

bear.t: Negative cash generation and financing risk
bear.b: Operating and free cash flow remain materially negative in TTM, so operations are not yet self-funded. Although cash burn is moving broadly in the right direction, consistently negative flows can require external financing and create dilution risk as the company scales.

Acquired HO is underdiagnosed and patients face physician education needs, long endocrinology wait times, and time-consuming diagnosis. These structural frictions can slow conversion of launch interest into reimbursed treatment, delaying revenue scaling even as awareness improves.
